extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers / referees for APS Physical Review journals
extracted.subtask_short: peer review for Physical Review journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for scientists serving as referees for American Physical Society (Physical Review) journals on how to evaluate submissions, structure reports, and follow ethical/confidentiality rules. Covers evaluation criteria, journal-specific standards, and responsibilities such as data and supplemental-material review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: are the claims and methods sound?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work's claims follow from the methods and evidence presented; ensure the research is valid, rigorous, and credible. Thorough and insightful reviews help authors improve their papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate originality of the contribution. Note that different APS journals place different emphasis on novelty (e.g., PRX and PRL expect higher novelty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: does it advance the field meaningfully?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the significance and potential impact of the results for the field; for highly selective journals emphasize broad significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of presentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, organization, and readability of the manuscript; identify areas where presentation could be improved to aid understanding and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the provided sections facilitates the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal-provided report sections and follow the specific guidelines for structuring your report to make evaluations clear and actionable for editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may comment on whether and how data are shared, though authors are ultimately responsible for data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the adequacy of data availability, transparency, and whether data sharing meets community/journal expectations; recommend appropriate data-availability statements or repositories when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether supplemental material is relevant to the main text and scientifically sound, and indicate whether any of it should be included in the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the relevance and scientific quality of supplemental files; flag material that is essential for understanding or validating results and recommend incorporating it into the main manuscript if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-specific acceptance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Different APS journals have different acceptance thresholds: Physical Review Letters: Highest selectivity; emphasis on broad significance and surprise; Physical Review X: Open access, highest novelty and impact; Physical Review A-E: Topical journals; technical excellence; Physical Review Research: Open access, broader scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust your assessment to the journal's stated threshold and mission — e.g., emphasize surprise and broad significance for PRL, highest novelty/impact for PRX, technical excellence for PRA–E, and broader scope for PR Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat manuscripts as confidential; do not share with non-reviewers; do not use information for personal advantage; do not contact authors directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality of manuscript content and reviewer identity per journal and ethical standards; avoid discussing manuscripts outside permitted editorial channels and do not exploit privileged information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For information on the proper conduct of referees, the APS recommends consulting the COPE Ethical Guidelines for Peer Reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE and APS guidance on conflicts of interest, confidentiality, fairness, and integrity in peer review; recuse yourself if conflicts prevent an objective review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities — role in upholding standards
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer, you play a crucial role in upholding the integrity of science by ensuring that published research is valid, rigorous, and credible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thorough, insightful reviews that help authors improve their papers while upholding the high standards of Physical Review; be fair, constructive, and timely in your evaluations.
